process_conclusion: The frontier-first approach produces cleaner, more efficient learning with decisive frontier progression and no redundant experiments.

The process-research alternation provides measurable methodological improvements through two key process tasks: cost sensitivity testing (Agent 02) and horizon sensitivity classification (Agent 04). However, these improvements come at the cost of additional orchestration complexity and artifacts. The information gain is real but partial - Agent 01's frontier audit would likely have been completed even without Agent 02/04. The pattern shows diminishing returns - each additional process task adds less marginal value than the previous.

The frontier-first approach produces cleaner, more efficient learning with decisive frontier progression and no redundant experiments. Transaction-cost robustness validation confirms the momentum edge survives realistic costs, strengthening the evidence case.
